thread:
Maria: Heads-up — getting a big spike of 429s from a single org (acme-prod) starting ~1865001200. CS is getting paged.
AJ: Saw it too, dashboard here: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/429s?org=acme-prod 
SRE Bot: Alert fired: quota_exhaustion_429_high (count=6123, 10m)
John: CS Oncall here — paging is noisy, can we suppress duplicates while we investigate? Customers are already annoyed. :grimacing:
Maria: Our current alert is on raw 429 rate, no smoothing. Suggest: switch to a rolling-percentile smoothing (5m median) + a short auto-suppress if autoscaler/rollback is triggered.
Liam: We have per-key burst buckets in the runtime, but alerting query doesn't reference them. That causes one big noisy org to flood alerts.
AJ: Proposal: change rule to require both: (1) smoothed_429_rate > threshold AND (2) sustained_unique_keys > 3 for 5m. That should cut single-key flapping.
Maria: Draft alert snippet I want to push (pseudo PromQL/AlertQL):
```
alert: QuotaExhaustion429High
expr: (rate(api_responses{code="429"}[1m]) > 0.05)
  and (quantile_over_time(0.5, rate(api_responses{code="429"}[5m])) > 0.03)
  and (count_over_time(distinct(api_key)[5m]) > 3)
for: 5m
annotations:
  runbook: "https://playbooks.redwood/quota-429"
  top_keys: query_top_keys(429,5m)
```
AJ: Also add an auto-mute tag so oncall can choose 10m suppress while we mitigate. SRE Bot can create a ticket automatically.
SRE Bot: Created ticket INF-4321: Investigate 429 flood from acme-prod.
John: I'll mute the channel for 10m and start customer comms. Please add an annotation with the offending top-5 keys so CS knows who to contact.
Maria: Will open a PR to update the alert rule and add an "offending_keys" annotation (top 5). I'll also add a panel to the 429 dashboard showing per-key burst buckets and quota consumption.
Liam: I can run a synthetic replay of the offending keys in staging to validate the new alert behavior. Targeting verification at 14:00 PT.
AJ: After PR, can we also add a brief note in the runbook for "temporary suppression" steps and the conditions under which CS should escalate?
John: Yes — I'll update the playbook with the suppression workflow and customer comms template.
Maria: I'll include a toggle in the alert to flip to "suppress on autoscale" (so if autoscaler scales up within 3m, we auto-suppress).
Liam: FYI the runtime emits a "burst_bucket" tag, we can join that in the dashboard query for quicker triage.
SRE Bot: Deploy job started: infra/alerts#patch-429-smoothing -> staging.
AJ: Ping when deployed, I'll run the dashboard checks.
SRE Bot: Deploy succeeded: infra/alerts#patch-429-smoothing -> staging (build 4821).
Maria: Deployed to staging. Verified: alert now requires rolling percentile + >3 unique keys. Triggered simulated flood and no page for single-key spike.
Liam: Synthetic replay passed, per-key panels show bucket fill and quick decay after autoscale.
John: CS: holding off on customer email until we confirm production change. Thanks team. :pray:
Maria: I'll cut the same change to prod after 30m of staging bake and update the runbook with screenshots.
John: Once prod change is live, I'll unmute and watch for regressions.
Maria: Filed follow-up ticket INF-4322 to add long-term metric: per-org 429 percentile baseline and daily regression alerts.
AJ: Nice. This should reduce alert noise significantly and give CS better triage data.
Maria: Closing thread for now — keep an eye on prod after rollout.
CS Oncall: Acknowledged, standing by.
